title: The 5 Oldest Spacecraft Still Working, Ranked (#1 Launched in 1977)

scenes.text: The five oldest spacecraft still working. Number one launched in 1977, and it still answers.

scenes.label: Hubble · 1990
scenes.text: Number five: Hubble, launched on the shuttle Discovery in April 1990. Nearly 1.7 million observations so far.

scenes.label: Wind · 1994
scenes.text: Number four: NASA's Wind, launched November 1994 to study the solar wind. Every instrument still works, with fuel for 50 more years.

scenes.label: SOHO · 1995
scenes.text: Number three: SOHO, launched December 1995 for a two-year mission. Thirty years on, it still watches the Sun and has found over 5,000 comets.

scenes.label: Voyager 1 · 1977
scenes.text: Number two: Voyager 1, September 1977. The farthest human-made object ever, so far that its signal takes most of a day to arrive.

scenes.label: Voyager 2 · 1977
scenes.text: Number one: Voyager 2, August 20, 1977, sixteen days before Voyager 1. The longest continuously operating spacecraft in deep space, nearly fifty years out.

description:
The five oldest spacecraft still operating, ranked by launch year.
Voyager 2 launched on 20 August 1977, sixteen days before Voyager 1, and the two Voyagers are the longest continuously operating spacecraft in deep space; SOHO (1995) was built for two years and has now watched the Sun for thirty while discovering over 5,000 comets; NASA's Wind (1994) still has every instrument working; Hubble (1990) has made nearly 1.7 million observations.
Which of these machines would you most want to keep alive?
first_comment: Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft that has ever visited Uranus and Neptune. Which would you put at number one, and what should we rank next?
